meta.title: Episode of vomiting blood
meta.candidate_brief: You are the medical registrar in the emergency department. Take an urgent focused history from this patient who has vomited blood and assess risk factors.

patient_script.opening_statement: I threw up and it was bright red blood earlier today.

if_asked.symptom_details: I felt nauseous this morning and when I vomited it was a large splash of bright red blood with some clots.
if_asked.timing: Happened three hours ago after a night of heavy drinking; before that I'd had a week of dark stools.
if_asked.after_effects: Since then I've felt dizzy and weak.
if_asked.exacerbating: When I stand up quickly the dizziness is worse.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: I've had black tarry stools this past week and mild upper tummy pain. No chest pain or fainting.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with alcohol-related liver disease two years ago; had a hospital stay for jaundice.
if_asked.medications: Take propranolol that the liver clinic gave me but I sometimes miss doses; also take omeprazole.
if_asked.allergies: Allergic to sulfa antibiotics; they make me swell up.
if_asked.family_history: Dad had cirrhosis from drinking. Mum has hypertension.
if_asked.social_history: I drink about half a bottle of whiskey most nights, smoke 10 cigarettes a day, live alone, and work part-time at a bar. No illicit drugs.
if_asked.functional_status: I've been missing shifts recently because I'm wiped out.

collateral.observer_note: Friend who brought him says he has been drinking heavily and looked pale for days.

pc.one_liner: I vomited a load of bright red blood a few hours back.

hpc.character: Large volume bright red blood with clots
hpc.timing: Single episode today with preceding week of melena

dh.recent_changes: Missed several propranolol doses over past week

sh.alcohol: Approximately 35 units per week, recent binge

ice.concerns: Afraid he might bleed to death
ice.expectations: Wants urgent help to stop the bleeding and guidance on what happens next

examiner_guidance.most_likely_diagnosis: Upper gastrointestinal bleed secondary to esophageal varices
immediate_investigations: Resuscitation with urgent bloods including FBC, U&E, coagulation
